elements.text: I had to refactor script to make this possible, which is what instigated the recent refactor. We’ve be holding the full script as a data vector, despite parsing it. This was because scripts can terminate in unparseable data. But this must be retained for serialization, as it’s valid if not executed (eg coinbase inputs). So we now have a flag in operation that indicates that the op is raw data for serialization. Originally this was attempted with a raw_data opcode, but this overloaded a potentially valid opcode. So now we can move to pointer stacks from deserialized pointer push-data ops.

elements.text: I’ve got another set of changes which move script, witness, input, output and transaction storage to shared_ptr, and a template for deriving their collections from std::vector, along with a template-defined ::ptr for the collection itself. These collection objects can be specialized to provide collection queries (such as obtaining the set of tx hashes), which will move a lot of code out of the primary objects.

elements.text: I’ve also removed all setters, making chain objects effectively const. Fabricating an object is possible, for tests and sighashing, by simply using initializer syntax with the property constructors. So with pointers, copy/move of existing objects into new objects becomes just a couple integer copies and pointer ref counts.
